name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: To achieve our goal of owning the visual presentation of the interface, I propose we prioritize a dark mode design, as it will enhance visibility and clarity, especially for users who work in low-light environments. This decision will also contribute to a more enjoyable experience, as dark mode can be easier on the eyes. By choosing to focus on dark mode, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially increased complexity in ensuring sufficient contrast and readability. This trade-off is worth it, as a well-designed dark mode will ultimately improve the overall visual presentation and user experience.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold on—dark mode’s great for low-light users, but what about the 30% of our audience who work in bright sunlight or glare-prone spaces? A light mode with high-contrast accents might actually improve visibility *more* for them. The real risk isn’t just preference; it’s alienating a sizable chunk of users if we default to dark mode without testing. Let’s settle this by running a quick A/B test with both modes and measuring readability metrics in different lighting conditions—no assumptions, just data.
